pure-announcement.rationale: This is Grafana's own launch post for its Pyroscope 2.0 release - the case-for-profiling and rearchitecture sections exist to sell the upgrade, and the piece closes with migration and GrafanaCON links rather than any product-independent method.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept (code graph, retrieval evals, MCP, SLO alerting, OSV) covers continuous profiling or profiling-database architecture.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The architectural claims and figures (write-path replication removed, 95% symbol-storage reduction, 19.5PB processed) are attributed to Grafana's production rollout and the open-source release a reader can inspect.

durability.rationale: The v1-vs-v2 feature deltas, rollout dates, and petabyte counts are release-bound, and even the reusable ideas (object storage as source of truth, stateless read path) are presented as this product's internals rather than as a general pattern.

actionability.rationale: The concrete steps it enables - upgrade to 2.0, provision object storage, follow the migration guide - are product-only actions rather than transferable build guidance.

atomicity.rationale: It interleaves two separable arguments - why continuous profiling belongs in the observability stack at all, and how the 2.0 rearchitecture cuts its cost - each aimed at a different reader.
